Substituting y=−log x gives exact moment integral retaining exp(−r y); omitting it yields the incorrect gamma term attributed in the record to printed Eq (5.9). For α=β=r=1,p=1/2, direct elementary integration gives E[X]=2log2−1 (strictly between 0 and1); the recorded published series substitution yields 2log2>1, impossible. For β=1, u=x^α gives the stated Gauss 2F1 expression and at α=2,p=1/2,r=1 exactly π/2−1. Independent mpmath quadrature agrees with the beta-one hypergeometric expression on multiple parameter choices. Formula Eq (5.14) formed by substituting false moment expressions likewise cannot be valid as written, though true MGF and its power series exist.
